the New Labour government was successful in raising standards across the system, but less so in reducing the inequalities of outcomes between different groups of learners.

, whilst there have been some successes in reducing educational inequalities, the overall picture is one of a system that is still failing many young people and which continues to be characterised by high levels of inequality.

, whilst there have been some important successes, the overall picture remains one of a system that is failing to deliver for many young people, particularly those from disadvantaged groups.

the English system is one that is characterised by an uneasy mixture of market-based and centrally driven interventions, and that it is a system in which there are many different policy ‘actors’, each with a distinctive policy ‘agenda’.
